# Resolved Meaning — Base-Data Spine Test (2 random verses × 66 books)

**Escalation:** #1596 (follow-on test, researcher instruction 2026-09-10)
**Date:** 2026-09-10 — **corrected same day**, see §0.
**Status:** demonstration/test run, not a deliverable pipeline — read-only against the DB; one new view (`vw_strong_gloss`) created.

## 0. Correction — the first version of this doc was wrong

The first pass answered a different, easier question than the one asked, and did it by going through code that shouldn't have been trusted. Researcher's own diagnosis, verbatim: *"a) what ever is in lexical at the moment is no longer valid. we are working towards redefining it, but that is still work in progress. b) there is no config defining resolved-sense, so you had to get the nearest match c) you resorted to resolve_code() which is still pointing to the faulty lexical methods, they have not yet been fixed... d) so this resulting in your whole answer being fraught with issues."*

What actually happened: `resolved_sense`'s `cfg_column.use` text ("stem/voice-selected sense text") is itself stale — reading it wasn't enough. I then substituted `strong_sense.head` (a different field, the code's general gloss, not a verse-specific resolution) without checking that substitution against anything. When asked to check what config actually says, I went one step further and read `lib/lexical.py:resolve_code()` directly — but that function is part of `verse_lexical`'s own build machinery, which the researcher had already ruled out as invalid and being redefined. Testing it live (not just reading it) showed why: for a base lemma with many senses (e.g. `H0430`, `G2192`), its fallback path joins every sense of the whole lemma into one undifferentiated wall of text — exactly the bloat escalation #1575 was raised to remove. Three separate missteps stacked on top of each other, not one.

**The corrected instruction, verbatim:** *"without going through any of the faulty code, configs and pointers, you should be able to solve my request by join verse, with span get all the strongs per verse from span, join with a parse construct (that consist of all three parse tables) and return the gloss column in the construct."* Below is that — a plain join, nothing else.

## 1. The process (corrected)

**New database object, per the researcher's own recommendation:** `vw_strong_gloss` — a view unioning `strong_meaning_parsed`, `strong_lsj_parsed`, and `strong_mounce_parsed` onto one uniform `gloss` column (the third table's own column is named `mounce_parsed`, aliased here). Built and committed live: `iba/app/migration/create_vw_strong_gloss_v1_20260910.py`.

```sql
CREATE VIEW vw_strong_gloss AS
SELECT strong_variant AS strong, 'meaning' AS source, sense_code AS sense_label, gloss,
       row_type, sort AS ord, id AS parse_id
FROM strong_meaning_parsed WHERE deleted=0
UNION ALL
SELECT strong AS strong, 'lsj' AS source, sense_label, gloss,
       row_type, id AS ord, id AS parse_id
FROM strong_lsj_parsed WHERE deleted=0
UNION ALL
SELECT strong AS strong, 'mounce' AS source, NULL AS sense_label, mounce_parsed AS gloss,
       row_type, id AS ord, id AS parse_id
FROM strong_mounce_parsed WHERE deleted=0
```

**Deliberately not a resolution mechanism.** No stem/voice narrowing, no base-lemma fallback, no ambiguity handling — every live sense row from every table, as-is, keyed on the *exact* code (`strong_variant`/`strong`, never `lemma_key`). If a code has no exact-match row, the view returns nothing for it — that's reported honestly below, not papered over.

**The query, per verse:**

```sql
SELECT sp.position, sp.surface, g.strong, g.source, g.sense_label, g.gloss
FROM verse v
JOIN span sp        ON sp.verse_id = v.id AND sp.deleted = 0
JOIN vw_strong_gloss g ON g.strong IN (<sp.strong_variant, split on space>)
WHERE v.id = ?
ORDER BY sp.position, g.source, g.ord
```

(the `IN (...)` step is done in Python here since `strong_variant` can hold more than one space-separated code per span row — SQLite has no clean native split; a real view/query built for this permanently would want a small carry-through table or a recursive-CTE splitter instead of ad-hoc string splitting.)

**Verse selection unchanged from the first pass** — same 132 verses (2 per book × 66 books), same seed (`random.Random(20260910)`), for a direct comparison.

## 2. The result — honest, including the gap

**132 verses, 2310 Strong's-code tokens.** **217 (9.4%) return ZERO gloss rows** via this exact-match join. 1492 return more than one row (multiple senses from one or more tables — no selection applied, all shown).

**The 217-token gap, checked, not left unexplained:** 77 distinct codes account for all of it. Every single one of them has real gloss data — just at their *base* lemma (`H0430`, not the `H0430G` a span actually carries), one letter short of what this strict join looks for. None are genuine "nothing exists anywhere" gaps in this sample. This is a real design question for `vw_strong_gloss` — whether a base-lemma-fallback pass belongs in this view, a second view, or stays out entirely — flagged here, not decided.

### 2John
